cases.name: text-value
cases.covers: The plainest write: a text field addressed by object number.

cases.name: text-empty
cases.covers: Emptying a text field, which is a value rather than an absence: the entry stays and reads back as an empty string.

cases.name: text-by-name
cases.covers: The same field addressed by its fully qualified name. A name reference exists for the fields that have no object number, and it resolves the ordinary ones too.

cases.name: text-reset
cases.covers: A reset puts the field back to its /DV, which here is a value that differs from both the current one and the empty string.

cases.name: text-reset-no-default
cases.covers: A reset on a field with no /DV. Nothing to go back to, so it empties rather than refusing.

cases.name: checkbox-off
cases.covers: Clearing a checkbox. The state is null rather than the string Off: one removes /V and the other names an appearance.

cases.name: checkbox-on
cases.covers: Checking it again by its export value, which on this fixture is Agree rather than Yes. A writer that assumed Yes would be refused.

cases.name: radio-switch
cases.covers: One write, TWO changed widgets: the one turning on and the one turning off. A value comparison alone cannot see the second.

cases.name: radio-clear-refused
cases.covers: Clearing a group whose /Ff has NoToggleToOff. The flag says a choice cannot be taken back once made, so PDFium refuses and the engine reports it rather than leaving the group in a state the flag forbids.

cases.name: toggle-on-text-refused
cases.covers: A toggle value aimed at a text field. Refused before any write, because the caller has confused two fields and PDFium would otherwise answer with the code it uses for a value the field could have held.

cases.name: direct-field-refused
cases.covers: A field stored as a direct dictionary in /AcroForm /Fields. The reader reports it, by name, because a document that holds one is not broken; the write API addresses a field by object number and a direct dictionary has none, so it is unwritable rather than missing.

cases.name: missing-field-refused
cases.covers: An object number no field has.

cases.name: unknown-toggle-state-refused
cases.covers: A state name the group has no widget for.

cases.name: combobox-free-text
cases.covers: A value that is none of the options, on a combo box whose /Ff has Edit. The flag is what makes it free text rather than a refusal, and the options come back with none selected.

cases.name: non-option-choice-refused
cases.covers: The same value against a LIST box, which has no Edit flag and therefore no free text: a value that is not one of its options is not a value it can hold.

cases.name: combobox-value
cases.covers: A combo box takes one of its options, by export value rather than by label.

cases.name: listbox-multi
cases.covers: A list box takes several at once, and reports them in option order rather than in the order they were sent.

cases.name: listbox-none
cases.covers: An empty selection, which is a list box with nothing chosen rather than a refused write.

documentCases.name: import-fdf-roundtrip
documentCases.covers: A document importing its own export. Every field is named and every value already matches, so nothing is skipped and the counts say the payload was understood.

documentCases.name: import-xfdf-roundtrip
documentCases.covers: The same through the other serialization.

documentCases.name: import-fdf-sniffed
documentCases.covers: The same payload with no declared format. FDF is a PDF-shaped file and XFDF is XML, so the first byte that is not whitespace decides, and a declaration that disagreed with the bytes would send the payload to the wrong parser.

documentCases.name: import-xfdf-sniffed
documentCases.covers: And the XML one, which the same byte tells apart.

documentCases.name: import-xfdf-changes-values
documentCases.covers: A payload that actually changes something, naming one field the document has and one it does not. The second is SKIPPED rather than failing: an export from one form legitimately names fields another lacks.

documentCases.name: import-xfdf-with-bom-sniffed
documentCases.covers: An XFDF payload behind a UTF-8 byte-order mark, which an exporter may write. The sniffer skips it; one that stopped at the first byte would send XML to the FDF parser.

documentCases.name: import-format-disagrees-refused
documentCases.covers: XFDF bytes declared as FDF. The declaration wins over the sniffer, which is what makes a wrong declaration visible: the payload goes to the parser the caller named and that parser says no.

documentCases.name: import-garbage-refused
documentCases.covers: Bytes that are neither. The sniffer sends them to the FDF parser, which says so.
documentCases.importText: this is not a form payload

documentCases.name: repair-plain
documentCases.covers: A repair on a form that is already consistent. Nothing to link, and the fixture asks for /NeedAppearances, which stays set because nothing baked a stream to replace it.

documentCases.name: repair-baking
documentCases.covers: The same with appearances baked. /NeedAppearances asks a viewer to draw the widgets itself, and once every widget has a stream of its own it is a request nobody needs to honour, so it can be cleared.
